summary: Apple's Face ID facial recognition on the iPhone X was reported to be unlockable by some identical twins of the registered owner. Apple itself acknowledged a different false-match probability for twins.
technical_summary: Face ID builds a mathematical face representation with a neural network and matches it at unlock. Near-identical facial geometry of identical twins can exceed the match threshold, producing a false accept and allowing unauthorized device access.

technology.quote: Mashable, on the other hand, found two sets of identical twins capable of thwarting Face ID.

failure_mode.quote: Mashable, on the other hand, found two sets of identical twins capable of thwarting Face ID.

notes: Reports disagree: one outlet's twin test did not fool Face ID. Only a demonstrated possibility, no realized harm.

summary: A court ordered the Sao Paulo metro operator to suspend a facial recognition surveillance system after civil society groups argued it would capture the faces of millions of riders without consent or transparency.
technical_summary: The metro planned to deploy the SecurOS video face biometrics platform across stations to capture and process riders' faces, with possible storage, sharing and integration with other surveillance systems. No consent mechanism, impact assessment or training-data disclosure was in place.
deployers: Companhia do Metropolitano de Sao Paulo

technology.quote: must immediately suspend the process to capture and processing of biometric data for facial recognition

failure_mode.quote: illegal and disproportionate, since all faces, from all users, will be read, copied, measured and recorded.
there is a lack of transparency around the characteristics and risks related to the treatment of personal data

harm_type.quote: illegal and disproportionate, since all faces, from all users, will be read, copied, measured and recorded.

notes: Rollout was halted by court order; extent of data actually captured is unclear.

summary: Patent filings and products from several Chinese tech firms were found to include facial recognition that detects ethnicity, including Uyghurs. Critics feared this would enable persecution and discrimination of a persecuted minority.
technical_summary: Facial recognition and pedestrian attribute analysis systems were developed with ethnicity classes, including a Uyghur label, per patents and cloud-service tests uncovered by IPVM. Such classifiers can be integrated into surveillance systems to flag members of an ethnic group.

technology.quote: developed a facial recognition algorithm that can identify a person

harm_type.quote: the persecution of the Muslim minority group spreads way beyond the Xinjiang Uighur Autonomous Region

lifecycle_stage.quote: Huawei, facial recognition firm Megvii, and several other Chinese tech firms have filed patents

affected_population.quote: the persecution of the Muslim minority group spreads way beyond the Xinjiang Uighur Autonomous Region

notes: Firms denied intent; Alibaba said its trial was not deployed by any customer. Harm largely prospective.

summary: A Dutch municipality set a home's tax value with a system it could not explain in court. The court noted a legal breach but still upheld the valuation because the result seemed reasonable.
technical_summary: A municipal property valuation (WOZ) model produced a home value that the municipality could not explain when challenged. Dutch case law and GDPR require explainability of automated decisions, yet the court accepted the opaque result as long as it was plausible.

failure_mode.quote: the municipality was unable to answer. Not because it did not want to, but because it could not.

notes: Excerpt says the claimant's challenge also rested on an unrelated earthquake-damage argument; AI use itself is uncertain.

summary: After a Taliban leader was found with a valid Pakistani ID card, Pakistan launched a nationwide biometric ID reverification. Many people, including long-term residents, had their cards blocked and lost access to services.
technical_summary: Pakistan's national biometric ID database (NADRA) was compromised by fraudulent registration. The response was a mass reverification that blocked or 'digitally impounded' cards, with little recourse, cutting people off from phones, welfare and other services.
developers: Pakistan National Database and Registration Authority
deployers: Pakistan National Database and Registration Authority

harm_type.quote: forcing 180 million people to prove that they were, in fact, Pakistani.
she was unable to access welfare programs that provided food rations, state-subsidized medicines and free schooling

notes: Harm stems mainly from the policy response (reverification) to a database compromise rather than an AI model error.

summary: A license plate reader flagged a family's minivan as matching a stolen motorcycle's plate. Police then held the family, including young children, at gunpoint and in handcuffs.
technical_summary: An automated license plate reader returned a hit matching the plate of a motorcycle reported stolen in Montana to a minivan. Officers acted on the hit without confirming the vehicle type, leading to a high-risk stop of an innocent family.

sector.quote: matched the license plate of a motorcycle from Montana that had been reported as stolen

failure_mode.quote: matched the license plate of a motorcycle from Montana that had been reported as stolen

harm_type.quote: four children between the ages of 6 and 17 facedown on the hot pavement, some of them in handcuffs

affected_population.quote: four children between the ages of 6 and 17 facedown on the hot pavement, some of them in handcuffs
a Black family with young children being menaced and traumatized by several cops

notes: Police said it was a system hit, not profiling; the vendor is unknown and the claim was not independently verified.

summary: A girls-only social app used facial recognition to verify users' gender, which excluded transgender women. Critics also raised concerns about bias against women of color and about sharing users' personal data.
technical_summary: The app sends a selfie to a third-party facial analysis service and admits users only if the model is about 95 percent confident they are female. This binary classification misclassifies trans women and may perform unevenly across races, while user data is shared with third parties.

technology.quote: uses facial recognition to determine if new users are male or female.

failure_mode.quote: decided to exclude trans women from the platform once trans activists began using it.
share that information with third-party websites and services, including facial recognition providers, chat room providers, and marketers.

notes: Exclusion of trans women was a stated design choice; the racial bias claims are allegations from critics.

summary: Amazon Flex contract drivers reported being fired by automated emails based on algorithmic performance ratings, including for factors outside their control, with little human review or chance to appeal.
technical_summary: Amazon's Flex platform tracked driver performance through automated metrics and issued terminations by email with minimal human oversight. Metrics penalized drivers for events like locked gates or flat tires, and the process offered no practical route to contest errors.
systems: Amazon Flex driver performance evaluation system

failure_mode.quote: This automation eliminates company personnel without even giving the opportunity to argue or defend themselves against robotic decisions.
machines are often the boss—hiring, rating and firingmillions of people with little or no human oversight

harm_type.quote: punished him for things beyond his control that prevented him from completing his deliveries

notes: Amazon's deliberate shift to automated management is the premise; individual terminations may be unintended errors.

summary: YouTube Kids showed children disturbing and inappropriate videos, such as familiar cartoon characters in violent scenes. Algorithmic filtering failed to catch them, and YouTube apologized.
technical_summary: YouTube Kids relied on algorithmic filtering and recommendation, plus user flagging, to screen content. Cheaply made videos using familiar characters evaded the filters and surfaced to young viewers before human review could remove them.

technology.quote: YouTube has been criticised for using algorithms to sieve through material rather than using human moderators to judge what might be appropriate.

failure_mode.quote: Investigators found several unsuitable videos including one of a burning aeroplane from the cartoon Paw Patrol

harm_type.quote: met five children who told her about the distressing videos they had seen on the site.

notes: Some content was deliberately produced by third parties to exploit the platform.

summary: A UN panel reported that a Turkish-made Kargu-2 drone with AI capability was used in Libya to hunt down and attack retreating fighters, possibly without direct human control. Casualties were not stated.
technical_summary: The Kargu-2 loitering munition uses machine learning and real-time image processing and can operate autonomously. Per the UN report, such systems were programmed to attack targets without a data link to the operator, a 'fire, forget and find' capability.

technology.quote: programmed to attack targets without requiring data connectivity between the operator and the munition

failure_mode.quote: programmed to attack targets without requiring data connectivity between the operator and the munition

harm_type.quote: were hunted down and remotely engaged by the unmanned combat aerial vehicles

notes: Reports say it is unclear whether anyone was killed or whether the drone truly acted without human control.

summary: Researchers found that roughly half the Twitter accounts discussing COVID-19, including many pushing to reopen America, appeared to be bots. They were artificially amplifying messages and inaccurate stories.
technical_summary: Researchers used AI classifiers on over 200 million tweets, flagging accounts by posting frequency, follower counts and apparent location. Coordinated bot networks and human-bot hybrids amplified COVID-19 messaging at roughly twice the usual bot share seen in contentious events.

failure_mode.quote: roughly half the accounts — including 62% of the 1,000 most influential retweeters — appeared to be bots

harm_type.quote: The researchers were able to categorize more than 100 types of inaccurate covid-19 stories

notes: Origins of the bot activity were not identified; researchers could not say whether it was domestic or foreign.

summary: Facebook removed posts and ads featuring famous historical artworks because of nudity, drawing complaints of cultural censorship from museums and tourism boards.
technical_summary: Facebook's nudity and adult-content policies, enforced through automated and human moderation, flagged classical paintings as sexual content and rejected promotional ads. The system could not distinguish art from prohibited nudity, and appeals were refused.
systems: Facebook content moderation and ad review

failure_mode.quote: Facebook took down a number of promotional ads for the Belgian region as they featured paintings of voluptuous women and cherubs.
Facebook said its decision was final

notes: Excerpts mix automated and human moderation; the share attributable to automation is unclear.
